system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: As of August 2026, may a female employee who has used her full maternity leave take further continuous leave to care for the child? If so, for how many days, in what circumstances, and what document must she produce? Answer briefly, covering all points.
raw_response: As of August 2026, under Thailand’s Labour Protection Act (amended in 2019), a female employee who has used her full 98 days of paid maternity leave may take an additional unpaid leave of up to 60 days to care for the child, making a total of up to 158 days of continuous leave. This extended leave is permitted only if the employer agrees. The employee must notify the employer in writing of her intention to take this additional leave and may be required to provide a medical certificate or other supporting document, such as a birth certificate, upon return. The right to return to the same position after this leave is protected by law.
